newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia bid seen sparking more - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Skandia bid seen sparking more - analysts.

text.p: A merger proposal by Swedish insurance firm Skandia and mortgage bank Stadshypotek, although still hanging in the air, signals the start of an industry-wide shake-up in Sweden's financial sector, analysts said on Monday.
The announcment, pending government approval, came in the wake of a statement that Sweden would sell its 34 percent Stadshypotek stake to an industrial buyer in a controlled auction.
Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink later on Monday criticised the proposal, saying he be would pursuing the original plan to sell it through an auction.

But no matter what the outcome of the race for Stadshypotek, analysts say the move triggered a long-awaited reshuffle of the Swedish and Nordic banking and insurance sector which is sure to end in fewer players.
"This is the beginning of an earthquake," Swedbank banking and insurance analyst Jonny Sylven told Reuters, saying the finance service sector shake-out could soon spread to major Nordic banks.

"Every bank has a lots of capital and the industry needs to develop. There are too many branches around the country," he said. "Everybody is talking about it, but no one really knows what will happen."
Shares in Skandia traded 7.5 crowns lower at 201 and Stadshypotek shares jumped 12 but fell back to trade six crowns higher at 204 after trade resumed following the news.
Elsewhere in the Nordic region, shares in Finnish banking group Merita Oy set a new 17-month high on strengthening hopes that Finnish insurer Pohjola and Skandia would move closer or merge.
Another banking analyst in Norway who asked not to be named said the key for insurance companies and banks in this crowded market was size.
"They're looking for economies of scale. Both on the cost side and on the question of capital base and the ability to absorb risks," he said.

"For example, with (Swedish insurers) Trygg and Wasa -- which was proposed a time back -- you'd see the operations basically overlap in cost structure. You could argue that you could run the merged groups on the cost basis of one company."
He said Skandia and Stadshypotek were an unlikely match, but agreed this was the beginning of industry-wide reshuffle.
"This is part of what you would call a shake-up and there's certainly going to be more transactions over the next few years," he said.
Carnegie analyst Per Griberg said a merger between Skandia and Stadshypotek would mean the launch of a new type of company on the Swedish market.

"It creates a new concept -- large financial institution combining banking and insurance products using sophisticated IT technology to distriubute them." Carnegie advised Skandia over the merger proposal.
The Norwegian analyst said investors were waiting for more changes on the Nordic market in the wake of Zurich Insurance Co of Switzerland's successful bid to takeover Norwegian insurer Protector ASA.

"You're seeing Trygg expanding in the Nordic region -- they're probably going to continue this. On the banking side -- you can list a number of potential deals in the Nordic region. There's going to be a number of deals."
Griberg said state-controlled Swedish bank Nordbanken and commercial S-E-Banken would probably be a part of future moves.
"Nordbanken and S-E-Banken -- that's not unlikely. S-E-Banken has been in discussions with a number of players.
Many other constellations have been mentioned in recent months, however, as the shake-up in over-banked Sweden dominated market gossip.

"Then there's Trygg Hansa -- will it merge with a bank or acquire another insurance company? And perhaps we will see cross-border merges here in the next few months. That's not impossible either," Griberg added.
